context_requirements: Cells must take up the compound and express ER/Golgi alpha-glucosidases (GANAB, GANC) or lysosomal GAA for glycoprotein processing to be inhibited.
A secretory or glycoprotein-dependent phenotype is needed for downstream transcriptional consequences.
Hepatocyte-like or intestinal-like metabolic machinery may be required for the cholesterol/lipid synthesis component.
falsifiers: No change in UPR/ER-stress landmark genes (e.g., XBP1, HERPUD1, DNAJB1) at 24 h in any line.
No coordinated decrease in cholesterol-synthesis genes at 24 h.
Strong, rapid (6 h) transcriptional changes inconsistent with slow glycoprotein-processing inhibition.
Line responses that do not track with secretory capacity or alpha-glucosidase expression.

evidence.supports: Alpha-glucosidase inhibition reduces beta1-integrin and FAK/ERK signaling in breast cancer cells, indicating effects on glycoprotein-dependent signaling.
Miglitol suppresses hyperglycemia-induced inflammatory cytokine gene expression in leukocytes.
Acarbose alters hepatic expression of PPARalpha, UCP2, ABCA1 and SREBP1c, linking alpha-glucosidase inhibition to lipid-metabolic transcription.
Miglitol changes bile acid metabolism and metabolic gene expression in diabetic mice.
Miglitol reduces inflammatory cytokine gene expression in peripheral leukocytes of type 2 diabetes patients.
